post.description:
Generates a pre-signed S3 URL that lets you upload an `.stl` file directly to storage, bypassing the API server entirely. Call this first - you need the returned `s3_key` to submit a quote.

## Upload Steps

1. Call this endpoint to receive an `upload_url` and `s3_key`.
2. `PUT` your STL file to `upload_url` with header `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`. **Maximum file size: 250 MB.**
3. Pass the `s3_key` to `POST /quotes` to start the pricing process.

The upload URL expires after 1 hour. After expiry you must call this endpoint again.

## Daily Quote Limit

A global daily limit on quote submissions is enforced to prevent abuse. Integration accounts are exempt from it. This endpoint is where the limit is checked and counted, since the quote record is created here. When a limit is active, successful responses include an `X-Daily-Quotes-Remaining` header with the number of quotes that can still be submitted today. Submitting once the limit is exhausted returns `429 Too Many Requests`. The limit resets at midnight.

201.description: Pre-signed URL ready. Upload your STL file to `upload_url` before it expires.

401.description: API key is missing or invalid.

403.description: The API key does not have permission to use quote endpoints.

429.description: Daily quote limit reached - try again tomorrow.

500.description: An unexpected error occurred on our side.

post.description:
Queues an uploaded STL file for automated price estimation. You must first obtain an `s3_key` by uploading the file via `POST /quotes/upload_file`.

The response includes a `publicId` you can use to poll `GET /quotes/:publicId` until `status` reaches `DONE` or `ERROR`. Alternatively, configure a webhook URL in the dashboard to receive a notification when processing completes.

## Webhook Notifications

When processing finishes, we send an HTTP `POST` to your configured webhook URL. Any `webhook_metadata` you attached to this request is echoed back unchanged in the payload.

### HMAC Signature Verification

Every webhook delivery includes two headers so you can verify authenticity:

- **`X-Dapi-Webhook-Signature`**: `sha256=<hex-digest>`
- **`X-Dapi-Webhook-Timestamp`**: Unix timestamp (seconds) when the payload was signed

**Verification steps:**

1. Read the raw request body as a UTF-8 string.
2. Concatenate: `{X-Dapi-Webhook-Timestamp}.{raw_body}`
3. Compute HMAC-SHA256 of that string using your webhook secret as the key.
4. Compare the hex digest with the value after `sha256=` in the signature header (use constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks).
5. Reject the payload if the timestamp is older than 5 minutes (replay protection).

### Webhook Payload Shape

```json
{
  "event": "quote.completed",
  "quote": {
    "public_id": "dapi_a3f9b2c1e4",
    "status": "DONE",
    "result": 12.34,
    "error_message": null
  },
  "webhook_metadata": { "order_id": "ORD-123", "notify": true },
  "timestamp": "2026-03-25T12:05:00.000Z"
}
```

### Expected Response

Return any `2xx` status code to acknowledge receipt. We retry on non-2xx responses.

post.description:
Places a new order by combining one or more completed quotes. Each item references a quote by its `publicId` and specifies the filament and quantity to produce.

**Prerequisites:**
- All referenced quotes must have `status` equal to `DONE`.
- All filament codes must be valid - retrieve available codes from `GET /orders/filaments`.
- At least one item is required.
- Each item lists its filaments in `filaments`, one code per colour slot in slot order; a single-colour design sends a one-element array.

**Multi-colour items:** `filaments` lists one code per colour slot in the design's own extruder order, so `["PLA-GREEN","PLA-RED"]` and `["PLA-RED","PLA-GREEN"]` order different products. Each distinct combination becomes its own SKU; repeating the same quote with the same combination reuses it.

The order is created with status `pending`. Use `POST /orders/:orderId/pay` to pay for it and move it into production.

400.description: Request body failed validation, a filament code is unrecognised, or a referenced quote does not have `status` `DONE`.

get.description:
Returns every shipping zone, the countries it covers as ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes, and the price of the first item in each weight tier plus each additional item.

**How a parcel is priced:**
- The tier comes from the HEAVIEST single item, not the summed weight of the order. Two small items ship as one Small plus one additional item, not as a Medium.
- Items under `extra_small_max_grams` are exempt from `additional_item_price`.
- A destination no zone lists falls to the zone with `catch_all` set.
- An order that cannot be rated at all is charged `flat_rate`.

Use `POST /orders/shipping/estimate` to price a specific order rather than deriving it.

Filaments are not accepted: colour does not change what a parcel weighs.

A destination that cannot be rated against the card is still priced - `shipping` is always what the order will be charged - but comes back with `zone` and `tier` null.

patch.description:
Moves an order belonging to your print farm to a new status. The print-farm transition matrix is intentionally tighter than the admin surface - only specific transitions are accepted, and any other change returns `400`.

Currently supported:
- `paid → in_production`
- `in_production → shipping` - requires `tracking_number` and `courier`. Pass `courier` as a code from `GET /print-farm/courier-options` (e.g. `ups`). For carriers not in the catalog, use `courier: "other"` together with `courier_name`; the order will be flagged for manual ShipStation sync.
- `shipping → returned` and `completed → returned` - no body fields beyond `status`. Triggers an internal admin notification; the customer is NOT emailed and no webhook is delivered.

Same-status requests are a no-op. Side effects (designer webhook delivery, customer status email, ShipStation mark-shipped on `shipping`, admin manual-sync alert when applicable, returned-order admin notification) fire after the DB update and never fail the request - check your webhook + email logs to verify. Requires an API key with the `WRITE_ORDERS` (or `FULL`) permission scope.

patch.description:
Increments `items_made` on a specific stock-level row by the given `quantity`. Transitions `pending → in_production` on the first non-zero increment, and `in_production → completed` when `items_made` reaches `stock_items_purchased` - completion also credits the farm wallet (one `payments` row, one `wallet.balance` bump) using `stock_level.manufacturer_price` as the payout amount.

Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header (any opaque string up to 255 chars) to make retries safe: a second request with the same key + body returns the cached response without re-executing. Same key with a different body returns `422`; an in-flight retry returns `409`.

Requires an API key with the `WRITE_STOCK` (or `FULL`) permission scope.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The public stock-level identifier (`slv_…`).

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Opaque caller-generated key (UUID recommended). When present, identical requests with the same key + body return the cached prior response without re-executing. Up to 255 characters.

requestBody.description: Quantity to add to `items_made` for this stock level.

200.description: The updated stock-level row.

400.description: Body validation failed, or the requested `quantity` would push `items_made` past `stock_items_purchased`.

403.description: The API key does not have the required permission scope.

404.description: No stock level with this `id` is allocated to your print farm.

409.description: The stock level is `consumed`, was modified concurrently, or another request with the same `Idempotency-Key` is already in flight.

422.description: `Idempotency-Key` reuse with a different request body, or the key exceeded the maximum length (255 chars).

429.description: Rate limit exceeded - wait until the window resets before retrying.

500.description: An unexpected error occurred on our side.

post.description:
Pay for a pending order. Three payment methods are available:

- **`wallet`**: Debit the order amount directly from your wallet balance. Fails if the balance is insufficient.
- **`wallet_auto`**: If wallet balance is insufficient, automatically top up from your saved card to the configured auto-topup amount, then debit.
- **`wallet_difference`**: If wallet balance is insufficient, automatically top up only the deficit from your saved card, then debit.

Both `wallet_auto` and `wallet_difference` require a saved card on your wallet.

This endpoint is idempotent - calling it on an already-paid order returns `409 Conflict`.

parameters.name: orderId
parameters.description: The unique order identifier returned when the order was created.

200.description: Payment successful. Order status is now `paid`.

400.description: Wallet balance is insufficient and no auto-topup is configured, or no saved card is on file for the selected payment method.

401.description: API key is missing or invalid.

402.description: Card charge failed. The payment could not be confirmed - verify your saved card details or add a new card via the dashboard.

403.description: The API key does not have permission to use order endpoints, or this order belongs to a different account.

404.description: No order with this `orderId` exists for your account.

409.description: The order has already been paid. No further action is needed.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded - wait until the window resets before retrying.

500.description: An unexpected error occurred on our side.

sales_price.description: Authoritative aggregate sales price for the stock (designer-set, admin-approved).

approval_status.description: Approval lifecycle status (e.g. pending, approved, rejected).

region_config.description: Per-region configuration. Each entry exposes the manufacturer price for the region.

extra_parts_config.description: Free-form extra parts configuration as stored on the stock.

created_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this stock was created.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this stock was last updated.

approved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when this stock was approved. Null when not yet approved.

stocks.description: Stocks on this page, sorted by creation date (newest first).

page.description: Page number returned, matching the `page` query parameter.

page_size.description: Number of items per page, matching the `page_size` query parameter.

total.description: Total number of stocks across all pages (after filters are applied).

code.description: Short courier code. Pass this value back when updating an order to `shipping`.

courier_options.description: All courier options available across configured ShipStation integrations.

paymentMethod.description:
How to fund the payment.

- `wallet` - deduct the full order amount from your wallet. Fails with `400` if the balance is insufficient.
- `wallet_auto` - if your wallet balance is too low, top it up from your saved card to the configured auto-topup target, then deduct. Requires a saved card.
- `wallet_difference` - if your wallet balance is too low, charge only the deficit to your saved card, then deduct. Requires a saved card.

orderId.description: Identifier of the order that was paid.

status.description: Order status after successful payment. Always `paid` on a `200` response.

topupAmountUsd.description: Amount in USD charged to your saved card as a wallet top-up. `0` when no top-up was needed because the wallet already had sufficient funds.

walletDebitedUsd.description: Amount in USD deducted from your wallet to settle the order.
